html:
SMTO-EXE-0011 — SMTO lost track of an earlier result this step needed

GUID: a72145cb-924e-4c59-93d0-cc67a665b65a
Slug: input-binding-authority-unavailable
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: exe

What happened

  • This step was set to reuse a result from an earlier step in the task, but SMTO couldn't find that saved result to check it. The step didn't run, so it changed nothing.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Select Copy error details in this panel and send them to the person who manages SMTO. This usually means part of SMTO didn't pass along the task's saved results, which needs a fix in SMTO itself.
  2. If you know the value the step needed (for example a file name or number from the earlier step), tell SMTO in the conversation and ask it to continue. With the real value in your message, the step no longer depends on the missing saved result.
  3. If you ask SMTO to redo the earlier step instead, first check whether that step already changed something, such as creating a file. Redoing a step that already made a change could make the change twice.

What success looks like

  • The step runs and shows its result in the task instead of this error.

If it still fails

  • If it happens again, start a new task with the same request and send the copied error details to the person who manages SMTO, noting what you asked for. Don't keep resending the same request in the same task; it will stop the same way.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Execution preflight could not resolve input_bindings because the invocation context lacked a callable receipt store, a prior-results mapping or a native run ID; the step was rejected before dispatch.

What this means

  • Input-binding preflight lacked a callable receipt store, prior-result mapping or nonempty owning run ID, so it could not validate authoritative source data. Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.

Why this can happen

  • Input-binding preflight lacked a callable receipt store, prior-result mapping or nonempty owning run ID, so it could not validate authoritative source data.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the internal invocation's native_receipts, native_results and native_run_id authority, separate from an individual missing result.

How to fix it

  • This is an internal context omission: find the caller of ExecutionEngine preflight that dispatched an invocation with input_bindings but without native_receipts, native_results or native_run_id, restore that context, and report a reproducible case. Never fabricate the bound value; issue a new operation once the owning run context is supplied.
  • Restore the owning run and receipt authority for the invocation; report a reproducible internal context omission. Never fabricate the missing input.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The consuming invocation has its owning receipt store and run context, and the referenced completed source validates.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
